findings.title: Storage payment-proofs SELECT policy specified only in prose, not SQL
findings.problem: The INSERT policy for storage.objects is given verbatim, but the SELECT policy that governs who can mint a signed URL for a payment screenshot (student owner / vendor owner / admin) is described only as 'the analogous exists predicate joining orders (and vendors for the owner branch)'. This is the access-control boundary for student-uploaded financial proof images; leaving it as prose risks an implementer forgetting to constrain the vendor-owner branch to vendors.owner_id = auth.uid(), which would let any vendor sign a URL for any order's screenshot.
findings.fix: Pin the SELECT policy as explicit SQL with the three authorized reader classes: student owner (orders.student_id = auth.uid()), vendor owner (join vendors where owner_id = auth.uid()), and public.auth_role() = 'admin', keyed off split_part(name,'/',1)::uuid, matching the already-verbatim INSERT policy.

findings.title: Admin OrdersPanel has no write scaffolding; reused run() helper lives in a different component
findings.problem: Verified in src/pages/Admin.jsx: the run() async-write helper (busy + setError + re-fetch) lives inside VendorRow (Vendors panel). OrdersPanel is a pure read-only table with no transitionOrder import, no busy/error state, and rows keyed by o.code. The design narrates the SELECT/row-key/button changes but never states OrdersPanel must grow its own write path, so 'reuse the existing run() helper' language misleads: OrdersPanel cannot reuse VendorRow.run (scoped to Vendors, writes via supabase.from('vendors')).
findings.fix: State in §4.5 that OrdersPanel must receive onChanged (=loadAll) and setError props like VendorsPanel/ReviewsPanel, import transitionOrder from ../lib/api, and implement its own per-row busy/reason/error handling. Note admin order writes go through the C# order service, unlike every existing admin write in that file.

findings.title: Widening StudentCancel auth to admin also grants admin cancel of plain pending orders
findings.problem: The StudentCancel branch classifies both pending->cancelled and the new awaiting_payment/payment_submitted->cancelled. Adding '|| admin' to that one branch necessarily lets an admin cancel a plain pending order too, which is not a stated requirement. Unflagged authorization widening.
findings.fix: Either explicitly accept and document that admins may cancel any StudentCancel-classified order, or scope the admin allowance to only the pre-payment from-states (plan.From is awaiting_payment or payment_submitted). State the choice.

findings.title: Endpoint-side screenshot-path validation not authoritatively pinned
findings.problem: The uuid-equals-route-id path check is correctly placed in the endpoint (not the pure service), but it is described twice with slightly different wording ('<uuid>/<name> shape, uuid equals route order id' vs '^<order-uuid>/.+') without a single authoritative statement of where it runs and what it returns.
findings.fix: State once that SubmitPaymentAsync (endpoint) rejects with 422 VALIDATION field=screenshotPath unless ScreenshotPath equals `{id}/{rest}` with non-empty rest and id the route GUID; keep reference-string rules in the pure ValidateSubmitPayment.
